title: Proof Repair Capability: Can LLMs Fix Broken Lean 4 Proofs After API Changes?

original_idea.body:
# Proof Repair Capability: Can LLMs Fix Broken Lean 4 Proofs After API Changes?

**Problem:** Real software evolves. When a library or API changes, previously verified proofs break. Whether LLMs can repair broken Lean 4 proofs automatically is unstudied.

**Direction:** Create a benchmark of 50 Lean 4 proofs that were valid under one version of a library but break under a newer version. Measure LLM success rate at repairing proofs. Compare to baseline (rewriting from scratch).

**Why it matters:** If proofs cannot be maintained after changes, formal verification is impractical for real software. LLM-assisted proof repair could be the key to making verified software maintainable.

**Relevant context:** CSLib roadmap (2026) includes expanding to undergraduate-level algorithms and data structures. Mathlib has a precedent of proof breakage during Lean version upgrades. Proof repair tools exist (e.g., CoqHammer) but LLM-based proof repair in Lean 4 is unstudied.
